newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged with firmer bias.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged with firmer bias.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were unchanged with a firmer bias on Monday as market participants marked time ahead of the Treasury's quarterly refunding, dealers said.

The only activity of note for corporates was moderate buying in the long end of the curve in anticipation of the 30-year roll to a new benchmark, traders said. The U.S. Treasury will sell $10.0 billion 30-year bonds on Thursday as part of its $39.75 quarterly refunding.
High-yields, meanwhile, were quiet with the exception of on large new issue from KinderCare Learning Centers.
Chase Securities raised the offering of senior subordinated notes due 2009 from $200 million to $300 million and priced them at par to yield 9.50 percent, sources said. The issue is rated B3/B-minus.

In the secondary, traders said bonds from OpTel Inc's $225 million overfunded senior note issue of Friday traded below par. The issue was priced to yield 13 percent, the wide side of price talk, and sold with warrants for five percent of the company.
Another trader said the bonds were trading at par.

Looking ahead, several high-yield issues were lined up for the week including $350 million from TCI Satellite Entertainment, $250 million from Globalstar, $175 million from Forcenergy and $110 million from Dawson Production Services.

NextWave Telecom Inc is rumored to be working up a $300 million debt offering via CIBC Wood Gundy and a related IPO through Smith Barney Inc and Lehman Brothers. Details were unavailable from CIBC, however.
High-yield secondary issues were mostly unchanged in light to moderate activity, traders said.

Neither the investment grade nor the high-yield market was able to derive any direction from U.S. Treasuries, which closed slightly lower ahead of the first leg of the government's quarterly refunding on Tuesday.
